messages:
infra-bot: Incident opened -> elevated error rates and model latency on dedicated-serving pool us-east-1. Detected 2024001111. Impact: dedicated customers and some hosted requests experiencing timeouts and 5xx from model backends. Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-8001 :rotating_light:

nina (oncall): seeing repeated `kernel panic - gpu driver fault` and `container OOM` on several g5 nodes in us-east-1; orchestrator is restarting pods and triggering model fallback to smaller quantized variants.

rachel: this started right after node image upgrade 2024000900 that included driver v525. Provider sent a driver patch that may be incompatible with our cuda runtime.

devops_lead: immediate mitigation plan: (1) cordon affected nodes, (2) drain and evacuate workloads to standby capacity in us-east-2 and west, (3) roll back node image to previous driver v520 via provider rollback API. Proceeding now. ETA ~25m.

support_ops: preparing customer bulletin: "We're investigating elevated latency and timeouts affecting dedicated-serving pools in us-east-1. Engineers are evacuating affected nodes and rolling driver rollback; fallbacks to smaller model variants are in effect to keep traffic online. Updates: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-8001."

nina (oncall): cordon started at 2024001180. Drain in waves to avoid thundering herd. Observability: request latency peaked 3x, error rate up to 14% for the pool.

sre_eng: can we confirm which model variants were used for fallback? Need to know for QoS and billing adjustments.

rachel: fallback mapping: large-4 -> large-4-quantized (reduced perf), large-8 -> large-4-quantized for critical requests; applied by routing policy to avoid OOM.

devops_lead: provider rollback initiated at 2024001300. Monitoring node restarts and kernel messages.

infra-bot: Mitigation update: node kernel panics reduced after rollback start. Model backend error rate for us-east-1 decreased from 14% -> 3% over 10m. Traffic draining ongoing.

nina (oncall): by 2024001405, evacuated 18/24 affected nodes; 6 remaining draining. Standby capacity absorbing ~70% of traffic; customers see degraded latency but fewer errors.

support_ops: customer note sent at 2024001420 to impacted accounts. Included link to status and temporary credit pledge for affected time window.

sre_eng: action items for RCA: (1) pin node image/driver versions in Dedicated IaC until compatibility test passes, (2) add preflight driver compatibility test in canary image rollout, (3) improve fallback routing transparency to expose which variant served each request for billing/telemetry, (4) add an alert when model backend error rate >10% for 5m.

rachel: provider confirmed the driver patch caused regressions on our CUDA runtime; provider SR-91200 opened. We're coordinating a durable remediation: avoid auto-upgrade channel and require staged canary for node images.

devops_lead: RCA owner assigned to rachel. Please publish draft RCA to /docs/incidents/INC-8001 within 72h. Keep incident open until rollback is validated in prod for 24h.

infra-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). Final update will be posted when RCA is available.
